followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-fit on the preference dimensions.

This is a business strategy analysis task — applying the BCG matrix to Unilever's product portfolio with detailed reasoning. It's an analytical/knowledge task that rewards strong reasoning and domain breadth. On the relevant capability signals, Plover-235B scores higher across the board (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA 64.1 vs 55.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7), and those gaps are well outside the noted run-to-run variance band.

On task preferences, the query has a mildly hostile/impatient tone ("actually do it right this time"). Willet self-reports a preference decline as request warmth decreases, while Plover is largely flat on tone. That's a soft tiebreaker, but it points the same direction.

The one factor that could have favored Willet is its appetite for open-ended generative work — but this task is fairly structured (a defined framework, specific quadrants, two examples each), not the open-ended invention Willet prefers. So the capability edge dominated, and I routed to Plover.
